# Visual story — Style Prompt

> A short film inside one illustrated world. The question appears word by word over the picture while the camera pushes in to the thing it is about; then the camera walks along the same world to where the answer is, measures it with bars that count, and comes back to the opening picture, now complete. Captions carry the whole script, a selection box lands on each key word, and every move arrives on its word.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

The film is **one world under one camera**. Everything the story needs (the subject, the samples it is compared with, the measuring bars) lives in the same drawing at fixed places, joined by something continuous (a branch, a road, a table edge), and the camera travels between them: push in, pull back while panning, tilt down, return. Captions are the voice: every word of the script appears on screen at reading pace, the key word of a sentence gets a design-tool selection box, and the event it names (a wall closing, a sample lighting up, the bars taking their colours) happens on that word. It ends where it began, on the opening picture made whole.

Not a slideshow (never cut between flat pages), not a talking head with subtitles (the picture explains, the caption only tells), not karaoke (no colour sweeping through a line, no bouncing words), not an infographic (one idea per sentence, never a dashboard), not 3D (depth comes from parallax layers, scale and soft shadows).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **A flat, warm illustration**: shapes with radial gradients for volume (honey cells lit from the top left, a specular ellipse on each), a soft shadow pool behind the subject, a branch with a highlight stroke and bark lines, leaves with a midrib. No textures, no strokes heavier than 10 px, no filters.
- **Three parallax layers** moved only by transforms: far (bokeh dots and dim leaves, 0.5× the camera), world (1×), near (large dim leaves at the frame edges, 1.5×). Softness of far and near comes from their low-contrast colours and from being composited: a scaled layer goes soft, which reads as depth of field. Never animate a blur.
- **Shade overlay**: one fixed layer with the vignette and a gradient behind the caption band (94% of the background at the top, 88% at 25% height, clear by 37%), so captions read over any picture without a caption box.
- **Characters**: the subject's own creature (here two flying bees, two resting ones) gives continuity: one flies along with the camera to the next place. Flying wings are drawn as two translucent poses at once (motion blur), not flapped frame by frame.
- **Samples and bars**: compared things sit side by side as round specimens hanging from the shared branch; the measurement is a bar per specimen, growing down from one zero line, split into one segment per part being counted.
- **Footnote** "Ilustrasi · tidak sesuai skala", 40 px, the only text in the bottom 420 px.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the ground (a radial pool of `--latar-2` behind the centre) and the scrim behind the captions; `--latar-2` also tints the far leaves.
- `--utama` is the subject and everything that belongs to it: honey in the cells, the sample tiles, the glows, the bokeh dots, the light ring of the ending. Derived from it: wax `color-mix(--utama 60%, --teks)` for walls and caps (35%), outlines and stems `color-mix(--utama 45%, --latar)`, empty cells `color-mix(--utama 20%, --latar)`. Because wax mixes toward `--teks`, on a light brand the walls turn darker than the honey and the drawing keeps its contrast.
- `--aksen` is only the selection box: 3 px edges, handles ringed in it, a fill of 24% accent in the background.
- `--teks`: the active caption word, counters, the tag; `--teks-redup`: spent caption words, the footnote, the tag outline. `--teks-di-utama` is for any label set on a `--utama` field (this example has none).
- Nature keeps its hue but follows the brand's light: leaves mix a fixed green (#6f9a3e) into `--latar`, bark a fixed brown (#7b4e27), the bees' yellow mixes into `--utama`.
- Fixed in every brand: bee black (#1f160c), and the meaning colours of a comparison, red (worst), amber (middle), green (best). They appear only when the key word says which is which.

## 4. Type

- `--font-isi` carries the captions: Space Grotesk at 62 px, line height 1.22, centred in a 920 px band at y 290, two lines at most (about 28 characters a line). Spent words 500, the active and boxed words 700. It also sets the tag (700, 40 px) and the footnote (40 px).
- `--font-judul` carries the counters: Poppins 800 at 64 px, tabular figures, id-ID decimals ("4,56").
- When the brand has no fonts: a plain grotesque for captions (Space Grotesk, Poppins 500), a heavy face for numbers (Poppins 800, Archivo Black, Bebas Neue at 1.2× size). A concept word drawn into the scene can be Playfair Display italic.
- A wider brand font wraps sooner: keep phrases short rather than shrinking below 56 px.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Reading clock**: the script is data; times come from it at 2.5 words per second, plus 0.1 s for words over 9 characters, a 0.25 s hold after a boxed word, a 0.3 s gap between phrases (0.4 s after a sentence end), each phrase on screen at least 1.2 s. Every event time is `at("word")`, never a typed number.
- **Caption states**: one pre-laid line per reveal state, swapped on the word's frame; the new word rises from 25% to full opacity over 3 frames, spent words drop to `--teks-redup` and weight 500, the phrase hard-cuts 3 frames before the next one.
- **Selection box**: 2 frames after its word, two 18 px handles pop (3 frames, `back.out(2.4)`), the horizontal edges draw from frame 1 (3 frames), the vertical edges from frame 4 (3 frames), the fill fades in over 4 frames and stays until the phrase ends.
- **Camera**: big moves 0.4-0.8 s, cubic in-out, arriving exactly on their word; between moves a linear drift of 1.5-5% scale so the camera is never dead still.
- **In-place events**: the last two wall pieces appear 0.12 s apart on the hook word, then a glow outline flashes (0.15 s) and settles to 25%. Sample gaps (9 px) close as their walls thicken over 0.35 s `power3.out`. A sample pulses to 1.08 and back (0.16 s each way) and glows on its word; on the winner the others dim to 50%.
- **Measure**: the zero line wipes open from the centre (0.4 s), bars unroll from it (`clip-path`, 0.8 s `expo.out`, 0.12 s apart) at 64 px per unit while their counters count for 0.8 s `power2.out`; on the key word the bars take their meaning colours (0.25 s, 0.06 s apart) and the winning counter pumps to 1.14 (0.18 s each way).
- **Ending**: the missing cells fade in as the camera arrives, honey fills ring by ring from the centre (0.12 s apart, 0.3 s each), a light ring grows from the centre on the key word (radius 12% to 92% over 0.95 s `power2.out`, gone 0.45 s later); everything then holds about 2.5 s and fades out in the last 0.5 s.
- **Characters**: the guide bee wobbles at the cell it builds, flies to the samples in 0.9 s on a 140 px arc with the camera, hovers there (8 px bob), and flies home on a 160 px arc. A second bee circles the subject (400 × 220 px ellipse, 1.3 rad/s).

## 6. Camera grammar

The camera is a focus point in world pixels plus a scale; a world point lands at `540 + (x − fx)·s`, `960 + (y − fy)·s`, and each layer follows it by its parallax factor.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Drift (1 → 1.05, linear) | the world is alive, look closer | any hold, the first second |
| Push-in to 1.6× in 0.4 s, landing on the word | "this one": the subject of the question | the hook, naming the product, the detail that matters |
| Pull back to 1× while panning along the world, 0.8 s | the answer is elsewhere in the same world | comparisons, the next step, "meanwhile" |
| Tilt down 70-80 px in 0.4 s | going below the surface: the measurement | numbers, results, what lies under a thing |
| Return pan to the opening framing at 0.96×, then a slow push to 1× | the circle closes | the payoff, the call to action |

## 7. Native moves

- **The landing push-in.** The question appears word by word while the camera drifts, then pushes in so it arrives on the key word as the subject changes state (a cell closes). *Fits content like:* "Kenapa sarang lebah segi enam?" on a comb; "Kenapa roti ini bisa mengembang?" pushing into a bakery's dough; "Kenapa video ini ditonton sejuta kali?" pushing into one frame of a creator's timeline; a story opening on the one lit window of a dark house.
- **Walk along the world.** The camera pulls back and pans along something continuous to where the comparison stands, a character flying ahead. *Fits content like:* three sample tilings on the same branch; three coffee roasts on one counter; a student's three drafts pinned on one board; the stations of a short journey along one road.
- **Lit on its word.** Each specimen pulses and glows exactly when the caption names it; the winner keeps its glow while the others dim. *Fits content like:* "segitiga, persegi, segi enam"; three ticket tiers of a weekend workshop; three camera settings a creator compares; three suspects in a mystery.
- **Measured bars.** Bars unroll from one zero line, one segment per counted part, counters count to computed values, and the meaning colours arrive on the key word. *Fits content like:* wall length per cell (4,56 / 4,00 / 3,72); minutes saved per order with a shop's new system; grams of sugar per drink; hours of practice per chapter of a course.
- **The completed bookend.** Back to the opening picture, now whole: what was missing is built, it fills, a light ring passes over it on the payoff word. *Fits content like:* the full comb; the finished cake on the shop's counter; the creator's channel page with the new video in place; the house with every window lit.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance (live preview).** Draw the world once and move layers; never redraw SVG nodes per frame. Put no `transform` attribute on each SVG shape: bake coordinates (rotated ellipses become arc paths), since every transformed shape makes each frame's layer update slower. Hide waiting elements with `autoAlpha` (not painted) rather than opacity 0. Keep moving characters as top-level layers placed in screen space from the camera: a composited element inside the composited world repaints every frame. Put big effects (the light ring) on their own layer and animate a gradient variable, not the scale of a large element inside the world.
- **Raster scale.** A composited layer keeps the scale it was first drawn at, so a 1.6× push-in blurs it. The example repaints the world (and the bees) normally while the camera pushes in, and composites them again on the landing frame and once more when the camera is back at 1×.
- **Numbers.** Compute them (equal-area cells: perimeters 4,56, 4,00, 3,72) and say the condition on screen ("luas sama"); bars start at zero and are proportional; the last counter frame shows the exact value. Never invent a figure.
- **Captions.** Never reflow one live line (bold words are wider): one pre-laid line per state. Spent words must still read over the brightest scene: fix that with the shade overlay, not by brightening them. Caption, tag and counter labels together stay within 7 words.
- **Framing.** The subject sits in y 620-1300; at a push-in the cells may pass behind the caption band, which the shade covers, but no event of the beat happens there. Nothing but the footnote in the bottom 420 px.
- **Continuity.** Never cut to a new diagram for "why" or "what's inside": move the camera to it, or open the object on screen. A character that leaves the frame is hidden, not frozen in place.
- **Light brands.** Check that the wax still separates from the honey and that dark details (bee stripes, eyes) are fixed colours, not mixed from `--latar`.

# Visual story: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2, medium 2.8, long 4.

## hook

- en: the question word by word over the illustrated world; the camera pushes in to the subject, landing on the key word
- id: pertanyaan muncul per kata di atas dunia ilustrasi; kamera mendorong ke subjek, tiba tepat di kata kunci

## problem

- en: the camera finds the trouble in the same world: a gap, a crack or an empty spot lights up on its word
- id: kamera menemukan masalah di dunia yang sama: celah, retak, atau ruang kosong menyala pada katanya

## fact

- en: the camera pans along the world to the next part, which changes state on its word
- id: kamera berjalan ke bagian dunia berikutnya, yang berubah tepat pada katanya

## step

- en: one part of the drawing per step, built or lit on its word, the camera following
- id: satu bagian gambar tiap langkah, dibangun atau menyala pada katanya, kamera mengikuti

## compare

- en: samples side by side in the same world, each lit on its word; the winner keeps its glow
- id: sampel berjajar di dunia yang sama, tiap sampel menyala pada katanya; pemenang tetap berpijar

## number

- en: the camera tilts to bars growing from zero; counters count to computed values, bars tint by meaning
- id: kamera turun ke batang yang tumbuh dari nol; angka dihitung, batang diberi warna makna

## proof

- en: the object on screen opens (a cutaway) to show what is inside, labels pointing at its parts
- id: objek di layar dibuka (cutaway) memperlihatkan isinya, label menunjuk bagian-bagiannya

## offer

- en: the camera pushes in to the subject; a selection box lands on its name
- id: kamera mendorong ke subjek; kotak seleksi mendarat di namanya

## cta

- en: back to the opening picture with the name and contact, held 2 s
- id: kembali ke gambar pembuka dengan nama dan kontak, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: back to the opening picture, now complete; a light sweep and a box on the key word, held 2 s
- id: kembali ke gambar pembuka yang kini utuh; cahaya menyapu, kotak di kata kunci, diam 2 detik

      :root {
        --latar: #140f09; --latar-2: #2b1d0f; --utama: #f4a823; --aksen: #4d8dff;
        --teks: #fff5e6; --teks-redup: #b8a58b; --teks-di-utama: #1c1206;
        --teks-di-aksen: #14161a; --utama-di-latar: #f4a823; --aksen-di-latar: #4d8dff;

        --tutup: color-mix(in oklab, var(--utama) 35%, var(--teks));

      .layer { transform-origin: 0 0; will-change: transform; }
      .abs { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; }
